To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of continuum models of the aqueous solvent can significantly speed up protein simulations and that (2) the use of simplified models for the protein itself can further increase the speed of simulations and can also provide a way to study protein folding.

the combination of molecular and continuum models is a promising approach to the simulation of protein molecules, and that the development of this approach requires a combination of scientific, engineering, and computational techniques.

(i) continuum models of the solvent can be used in conjunction with atomistic models of the protein to study protein-solvent interactions, (ii) the use of a continuum model of the solvent allows one to study longer time scales, and (iii) in order to study protein-solute interactions in conjunction with the solvent, one will need to develop simplified models of the protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing new computational methods to study the structure and dynamics of proteins.
the development of methods for simulating complex systems.

the following issues: the development of continuum models of the protein itself; the development of continuum descriptions of the solvent; and the development of software engineering techniques to facilitate combining these different models.

the future of protein modeling is bright.
the use of continuum models for proteins will be a very important area of research in the future.

we have been able to combine a continuum model of the solvent and the protein with a detailed atomic model of the active site of an enzyme in a single simulation.

it is possible to use continuum methods to study protein dynamics on time scales that are inaccessible to atomistic simulations.
